findings.finding: SAFE_ERROR_TYPES is used when summarizing input fields, but caught exception class names in the errors list and outer failure summary are emitted directly. For example, malformed JSON may yield the fixed class name JSONDecodeError, which is outside SAFE_ERROR_TYPES. This does not echo the exception message or file contents, but the declared error-label domain is not applied consistently.

anchors.excerpt: except (OSError, ValueError, RecursionError, Refused) as error:

accepted: R1 F1: input-derived schema/status/phase/reason/guard/resource labels are emitted only from finite sets or as UNCLASSIFIED_DIAGNOSTIC_LABEL; arbitrary input text is not forwarded.

R1 F2: launch.owner is required to be an object before attempt_id is read; the attempt path is regex constrained, and Refused is captured as bounded error metadata after executable facts are collected.

R1 F3: output ancestry is opened without following symlinks; leaf creation is O_EXCL/O_NOFOLLOW; write loop, fchmod 0400, fsync, held leaf/path identity, parent/output namespace identity re-open, and final identity checks precede success.
R1 N1: strict sys.executable resolution occurs inside its own role try; OSError/Refused are recorded per role so /bin/ps metadata collection can continue.
No subprocess, runtime/source execution, recursion, target receipt body output, or qualification inference is present in the reviewed source.
coverage: Static read of all 379 source lines and all top-level functions/entrypoint; finite label provenance and declared R1 findings/change record cross-checked as data.
qualification: Source-only review. No import, compile, test, helper, CI, runtime, native, process, network, or metadata-reader execution. No actual diagnostic output or retained artifact verified.
